newsitem.title: FRANCE: France presses Taleban to release aid workers.
newsitem.headline: France presses Taleban to release aid workers.

text.p: France pledged on Tuesday to do all it could to obtain the release of two French aid workers held by the Islamic Taleban in Afghanistan.
"We are in contact with the local authorities, the United Nations and all other parties in a position to help," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
Rummelhardt added that Paris's charge d'affaires in Afghanistan Didier Leroy had been allowed to visit aid workers Frederich Michel and Jose Daniel Llorente after repeated demands.
"They are in good health and good spirits," the spokesman told reporters at the Foreign Ministry's regular daily news briefing.

The two Frenchmen from the Paris-based group Action Contre la Faim (Action Against Hunger) were arrested over the weekend after a series of incidents in which Taleban militia broke into U.N. headquarters, allegedly to make sure their purist agenda was being followed.

In Kabul, the Taleban's information minister, Amir Khan Mutaqi, said the Frenchmen were being interrogated "to see what crimes have been committted." He said they had "trampled underfoot Islamic and international moral principles."
Action Contre la Faim's foreign staff has since left Kabul for Pakistan.
The United Nations has warned the Tableban that Afghanistan could lose humanitarian assistance if it did not release the aid workers immediately.
